summary: @servicetitan/design-system preinstall fetches Bun runtime to execute undeclared obfuscated payload
details: The package declares a preinstall script `node setup.mjs`. `setup.mjs` is source-obfuscated (hex-named identifiers, string-array lookup wrappers) and at install time downloads the Bun runtime from `github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/<archive>.zip`, unpacks it, then invokes the downloaded Bun binary via `execFileSync(bunPath, [<math_init.js path>], {stdio:"inherit"})` against a sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 711 KB `// @bun @bun-cjs` bundle with a rotating string-array decoder and a mixed-alphabet decode table — the standard shape of a packed loader. The file sits at the tarball root but is not listed in `package.json` `files` (which declares only `dist` and `readme.md`), so it is not part of the advertised published surface. The alternate-runtime-dropper pattern — routing install-time execution through a freshly-fetched non-Node runtime to execute an undeclared, heavily obfuscated bundled payload — runs attacker-controlled code on the installer's machine at `npm install` time under the installer's privileges. A React design-system UI library has no legitimate need to fetch a second language runtime and execute an obfuscated blob during install. The `@servicetitan` scope and version pattern are consistent with the recent scope-hijack / typosquat wave targeting internal-brand npm scopes.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
